title: Why Your Gains Stalled (It's Not Your Program)
creator: Coach Dani Reyes
description:
You switched programs three times and you're still stuck. Here are the four things I check with every client before touching their training.

Coaching applications: https://danireyescoaching.com
Instagram: @coachdanireyes

sentences.t: If your lifts haven't moved in two months, I promise you the answer is probably not a new program.
I've coached a few hundred people at this point, and when somebody stalls, there are four things I check before I change a single set or rep.
Number one is food, and specifically protein.
Most people I start working with are eating maybe half the protein they think they are.
Track it honestly for one week, not forever, just one week, and I bet you'll be surprised.
Somewhere around point seven to one gram per pound of bodyweight is where I want most of my clients.
Number two is effort.
If you finish every set feeling like you could have done six more reps, that's not training, that's rehearsal.
You don't need to go to failure on everything, but most of your working sets should end within two or three reps of it.
Film yourself, because the last rep you think was a grinder usually looks pretty easy on video.
Number three is sleep, and this is the one people roll their eyes at.
A couple of years ago I looked back through my client check-ins, and the pattern was honestly kind of shocking.
The guys who were sleeping under six hours basically stopped progressing, even on a perfect program.
And that's actually a big part of why I started tracking my own sleep last year.
This part of the video is brought to you by Somna, which is the sleep ring I've been wearing every single night since.
It's this little titanium ring, you forget it's on, and in the morning it tells you how long you actually slept, how much of it was deep sleep, and what your resting heart rate did.
For me the big eye-opener was that my two late-night coffees were wrecking my deep sleep, even though I fell asleep fine.
Cut those out, deep sleep went up, and my squat started moving again.
There's no monthly subscription, and the battery lasts about a week.
If you want one, code DANI gets you forty dollars off at somnaring.com.
Okay, number four, and this is the big one.
Consistency over months, not weeks.
A lot of people say they've been stuck for two months, and then we look at their log and they trained maybe five weeks of those eight.
Life happens, that's fine, but a stall you caused by missing sessions isn't a programming problem.
What I tell clients is, I'd rather you train three days a week every week than five days a week when you feel like it.
Pick a schedule you could keep even during a bad week, and treat it like a meeting you can't cancel.
Once all four of those are dialed in, then sure, let's talk about your program.
Maybe you need more volume, maybe you need a deload, maybe you need to rotate some exercises for hypertrophy.
But I'd say eight times out of ten, by the time we fix food, effort, sleep and consistency, the old program starts working again.
So before you buy another spreadsheet off the internet, go through those four honestly.
